this paper provides an overview of the new provisions of the General Data Protection regulation (GDPR) concerning Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) and proposes a process for their implementation, taking into account the requirements of the legislation and the needs of controllers.
the GDPR is not a new regulation, but an update of the Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC.

the GDPR is an important step forward to ensure that data protection is taken into account at an early stage of the development of products and services.
the GDPR is a step towards more protection of data subjects and more accountability of the data controllers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GDPR’s Data Protection Impact Assessment is a process which should not only be conducted at the beginning of a project, but also be a continuous process which is adapted as new data processing operations are added to the project.
the process should be designed in a way that it can be adapted to the specific circumstances of a controller.
the process should be seen as part of the controller’s data protection management system and should be embedded into its data protection governance.
